label: ex:cosmological-limits
title: Cosmological limits of $q$
html:
Conjectural interpretation. The parameter range of the substrate field q models a cosmological trajectory for a quantum observable universe. The limits of q represent a "big bang" and a "heat death".

Consider M = S^3 equipped with the standard contact form \varTheta and the standard instanton on the Hopf bundle. As the instanton curvature concentrates near a point p_0 \in S^3, the substrate field q partitions into two regimes:

  • Near p_0 (q(p) \to \infty, \hbar_q \to 1): Uncertainty becomes maximal ([\hat{X},\hat{P}]_q \to J). Observables become maximally non-commutative. The quantum observable universe becomes fully quantum-mechanical, retaining no classical shadow. This is the "big bang" regime.

  • Away from p_0 (q(p) \to 1, \hbar_q \to 0): The commutator [\hat{X}, \hat{P}]_q vanishes. The Hopf algebra becomes cocommutative (\sigma \circ \Delta = \Delta). Observations commute, q-deformed operators reduce to their classical limits, and the transport equation reduces to classical parallel transport (\nabla\psi = 0). This is the "heat death" regime: a fully classical, frozen universe.

At both limits, the quantum observable universe structure degenerates:

  • As q \to \infty, the Frobenius pairing \langle f, g \rangle = \int_A(\mu(f \otimes g)) loses non-degeneracy. Axiom (1) of the definition of a quantum observable universe fails. The universe ceases to be observable.

  • As q \to 1, the q-Hodge star \star_q reduces to the classical Hodge star \star_1. The quantum gauge group \mathrm{SU}_q(2) collapses to the classical Lie group \mathrm{SU}(2). The deformation vanishes, and the substrate parameter carries no information.

We conjecture the physically meaningful regime strictly satisfies 1 < q < \infty, where quantum and classical features coexist. Rigorously analyzing these limits requires controlling the singular behavior of the Frobenius form as q \to \infty. This remains an open problem.
